memos.headline: S04 and S10 lead on relative strength; S02 and S09 in structural downtrends to avoid
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation across the universe today. S04 is the standout leader—trading just 1.5% off its 52-week high, +12.5% above its 50-day mean, +10.4% above its 200-day mean, with RSI at 69.8 and 12-week relative strength vs SPY of +13.7%; the only risk is near-term overbought exhaustion, but trend deserves respect. S10 has surged +21.1% over four weeks with +15.5% relative strength vs SPY, though its 3.62% ATR and still -8.1% over 26 weeks suggest this is a momentum recovery rather than a confirmed new uptrend—I'd need to see it hold above its 50-day mean (~116 area) to stay constructive. On the downside, S02 is in freefall: -51.7% from its 52-week high, RSI 30.3, 30.5% below its 50-day mean, and -37.7% relative strength vs SPY over 12 weeks—this is a broken chart with no sign of basing. S09 is similarly weak at RSI 38.1, -9.1% below its 200-day mean, and negative relative strength across all timeframes; I'd need a reclaim above the 200-day mean (~112) to reconsider.

views.note: Strongest trend in the universe: near 52-week highs, well above both moving averages, +13.7% 12w relative strength vs SPY; would reassess on a close below the 50-day mean (~410 area).
Explosive 4-week +21.1% rally with best 4-week relative strength (+15.5% vs SPY), but high ATR of 3.62% and still negative on 26-week return warrant smaller sizing; invalidated below ~116.
Steady uptrend with +10.4% above 200-day mean, only -5.7% from highs, low ATR of 1.79%, and positive relative strength across timeframes; would cut below the 200-day mean (~239 area).
Close to 52-week high (-5.5%) and above both moving averages, but 12-week relative strength vs SPY is -3.8%, suggesting it's merely keeping pace; no edge either way.
Strong 4-week bounce of +10.9% but still -2.8% below 200-day mean and -16.5% from highs; needs to reclaim the 200-day (~358) to turn bullish.
Persistent weakness: -22.5% from highs, -11.0% below 200-day mean, negative relative strength of -15.9% over 12 weeks; no sign of a bottom forming.
RSI 38.1, -9.1% below 200-day mean, -18.4% drawdown, and negative relative strength across all timeframes; would need a close above ~112 to reconsider.
Catastrophic breakdown: -51.7% from highs, RSI 30.3, -42.2% below 200-day mean, 7.07% ATR—this is a falling knife with no technical support visible.

memos.headline: S10 and S05 Lead on Earnings Power; S07 and S09 Flash Warning Signs on Margin and Growth
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe between durable, high-margin compounders and names showing cash-flow compression risk. S10 stands out with 69.2% YoY revenue growth, a 42.6% net margin, and only $8.46B in total debt — the cleanest balance sheet in the group. S05 posted 38.3% net margins on $90.23B of revenue with net income up 46.0% YoY, which is exceptional operating leverage. On the other end, S07 is contracting: revenue fell 9.8% YoY and net income dropped 29.8%, while carrying $31.74B in debt against just $14.25B in quarterly revenue — I need to see a revenue stabilization before getting constructive. S09 is similarly concerning with flat revenue (+0.1%) and a 6.2% decline in net income on a thin 9.3% margin; any further margin erosion would make this an outright avoid.

views.note: 69.2% YoY revenue growth, 42.6% net margin, and minimal leverage ($8.46B debt) represent best-in-class earnings power; would reassess if margins compress below 35%.
38.3% net margin with 46% YoY net income growth on $90.23B revenue and only $14.79B debt signals durable, capital-light earnings; watch for revenue deceleration below high single digits.
36.9% net margin and 17.7% YoY net income growth on $70.07B revenue with manageable $42.88B debt is a strong profile; would trim if margin dips below 30%.
Revenue of $155.67B grew 8.6% YoY and net income surged 64.2%, but the 11.0% net margin and $58.75B debt leave limited room for error; need to see margin expansion sustain.

Solid 26.0% net margin on $95.36B revenue but only 5.1% top-line growth and $92.20B in debt suggest mature, leveraged earnings; would get more constructive if revenue reaccelerates above mid-single digits.
32.3% net margin is attractive but $407.22B in total debt dwarfs the $45.31B quarterly revenue; leverage profile demands a premium for risk.
Flat revenue (+0.1% YoY), declining net income (-6.2%), and a thin 9.3% margin on $32.82B debt signal earnings compression; would reconsider only if margins recover above 11%.
Revenue down 9.8% YoY and net income down 29.8% with $31.74B debt against $14.25B quarterly revenue is a deteriorating fundamental picture; need revenue stabilization before engaging.
9.8% revenue growth is decent but 5.7% net margin on $109.58B revenue with $81.27B debt is razor-thin; net income YoY not available, limiting visibility.
19.1% net margin is respectable but revenue declined 2.1% YoY and net income was essentially flat (+0.4%); $24.25B debt on $19.78B quarterly revenue warrants caution until top-line inflects.

memos.headline: Fed on Hold at 4.50% With Softening Labor Market and Benign CPI — Favor Duration-Sensitive Growth Over Cyclicals
memos.body: I see the macro regime as a prolonged pause with an easing bias: the Fed has held the upper bound at 4.50% for three months while the 12-month change is -100bp, CPI is running at just 2.3% YoY, and unemployment has drifted up 30bp over the past year to 4.2%. The 10y-2y spread has steepened sharply (+86bp YoY to +0.51pp), consistent with the market pricing eventual cuts, though the 10y yield itself has risen 17bp over three months to 4.41%, suggesting term premium or fiscal concerns are keeping the long end elevated. I have moderate conviction that this pause-to-easing backdrop favors duration-sensitive growth and defensive staples while being less supportive for banks (whose NIM benefit from curve steepening may be offset by slowing loan demand) and pure cyclicals exposed to a softening labor market. A surprise CPI print above 3% or unemployment dropping back below 3.9% would force me to revisit the easing-bias call.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth benefits from an easing-bias regime with 2.3% CPI and a steepening curve signaling rate cuts ahead.
Defensive staples should outperform as unemployment rises (+0.30 YoY) and the economy softens under a prolonged pause.
Banks benefit from the 51bp positive 10y-2y spread but face headwinds from rising unemployment and potential credit deterioration.
Cyclicals look vulnerable as unemployment trends higher and the Fed remains on hold, signaling no near-term stimulus impulse.
Energy lacks a clear macro tailwind; benign inflation and softening demand indicators keep me sidelined.
Growth-oriented names with duration exposure should re-rate as the market prices in cuts from the current 4.50% hold.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: S04 and S10 Positive Momentum vs. S02 and S08 Negative Overhang
memos.body: I see a clear split in post-earnings sentiment across the universe. S04 posted a +7.6% earnings-day reaction on 4/30 and S10 just printed +3.2% on its 5/28 results, suggesting positive narrative momentum that may not yet be fully priced given the recency of S10's report. On the negative side, S02 suffered a brutal -22.4% earnings-day drop on 4/17 followed by three separate director departure/appointment 8-Ks in quick succession—a pattern that signals ongoing management turmoil and likely sustained negative tone. S08 dropped -3.7% on its 5/1 earnings and has had no positive catalyst since, while S01 also fell -3.7% on its Q3 results. I have highest conviction on S10 as a fresh positive inflection and on S02 as an avoid given the compounding negative signals.

views.note: Strong +7.6% earnings reaction on 4/30 suggests positive sentiment shift; no subsequent negative filings to reverse the narrative.
Fresh +3.2% earnings reaction just two days ago on 5/28 indicates positive tone inflection that is unlikely fully priced yet.
The -22.4% earnings crash on 4/17 combined with three director departure/appointment filings in five weeks signals deep management instability and persistently negative sentiment.
Earnings-day -3.7% drop on 5/1 with only a generic Other Events filing since; no evidence of tone recovery.
Solid +4.0% earnings reaction on 4/11 and steady flow of Reg FD and shareholder vote filings suggest constructive engagement, though the move is six weeks old and may be priced.
Q3 earnings drove a -3.7% drop on 4/24 and subsequent filings are routine; no positive tone shift visible.
Mild +1.7% earnings reaction on 4/24 followed by multiple Other Events filings—steady but unremarkable sentiment.
Flat +0.4% earnings reaction on 5/2 with no follow-up filings; sentiment is a non-event.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Retreating Fast but Still Elevated; Oil Weakness Signals Demand-Side Geopolitical Risk Repricing
memos.body: I note that the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index has plunged 41% over the past month to 340, yet remains only 1.5% below its level three months ago, suggesting the acute tariff/sanctions shock of early spring is fading but structural policy risk persists. VIX at 19.18 (down 21% m/m) and HY OAS tightening 52 bp in a month confirm markets are pricing a calmer near-term policy backdrop. WTI crude at $61.66, down nearly 12% over three months, points to either softening global demand expectations or easing supply-side geopolitical premia—either reading is bearish for energy-exposed names and modestly supportive for energy-consuming industrials. Without granular detail in the 8-K filings beyond item codes, I have limited company-specific conviction; my views lean on macro-policy signals and filing frequency as a proxy for event intensity. A re-escalation of export controls or new sanctions on China would be the key catalyst that changes my stance on tech-exposed and energy names.

views.note: Four 8-K filings in three weeks (Apr-May) suggest elevated corporate event activity that could reflect policy-driven restructuring; I lack detail to take a directional view.
Four filings across April-May including Reg FD disclosures hint at active investor communication amid policy flux; the drop in uncertainty is supportive but I need more specifics.
Declining policy uncertainty and tighter credit spreads favor large-cap quality; three filings suggest proactive disclosure, and the macro backdrop is improving.
Single 8-K in May provides little signal; the easing VIX and policy uncertainty are mildly supportive but I have no company-specific geopolitical edge.
WTI down 12% in three months signals weakening energy/commodity demand expectations; if S10 has commodity exposure, the geopolitical demand repricing is a headwind.
Two filings in quick succession and a rapidly improving policy-uncertainty backdrop suggest the company is navigating the environment actively; credit conditions are supportive.

plan.summary: Concentrate in S04 and S10 where technical momentum, fundamentals, and sentiment converge positively, with supporting positions in S06 and S05 for diversification. Hold ~20% cash as a buffer against overbought exhaustion in leaders and residual macro uncertainty.

plans.rationale: Strongest consensus across all analysts: near 52-week highs with +13.7% 12w relative strength (Technical), 36.9% net margin with 17.7% income growth (Fundamentals), and a +7.6% earnings-day pop with no negative follow-through (Sentiment). Only risk is near-term overbought RSI ~70.
plans.changes_my_mind: A weekly close below the 50-day moving average (~410 area) or RSI divergence on new highs would signal exhaustion and invalidate the trend thesis.

plans.rationale: Best fundamental profile in the universe (69.2% revenue growth, 42.6% net margin, clean balance sheet) confirmed by a fresh +3.2% earnings reaction on 5/28 (Sentiment) and explosive +21.1% 4-week rally (Technical). Sized slightly below S04 due to higher ATR (3.62%) and still-negative 26-week return. Geopolitics analyst flagged commodity-demand concern but fundamentals clearly dominate.
plans.changes_my_mind: A close below the 50-day mean (~116) would break the recovery structure; net margin compressing below 35% on next report would undermine the fundamental case.

plans.rationale: Steady uptrend with low volatility (1.79% ATR), +10.4% above 200-day mean, and positive relative strength (Technical). Sentiment is constructive with a +4.0% earnings reaction, though six weeks old. Fundamentals show a solid 32.3% net margin but heavy debt ($407B) tempers conviction. Serves as a lower-beta diversifier.
plans.changes_my_mind: A close below the 200-day moving average (~239) would negate the uptrend; any credit-rating downgrade or debt-covenant concern would amplify the leverage risk.

plans.rationale: Exceptional earnings power (38.3% net margin, 46% YoY net income growth) on a capital-light model with minimal debt (Fundamentals). Sentiment is neutral-to-mildly-positive (+1.7% earnings reaction). Technical and macro analysts are neutral, so sizing is moderate. Macro analyst notes banks face mixed signals from steepening curve vs. rising unemployment.
plans.changes_my_mind: Revenue deceleration below high-single-digit growth or a negative earnings revision cycle would undermine the growth premium thesis.

plans.rationale: Macro analyst favors defensive staples in a softening labor market; fundamentals show 8.6% revenue growth and 64.2% net income surge, though thin 11% margin and $58.75B debt limit upside. No strong technical or sentiment signal, so kept as a small diversifying position.
plans.changes_my_mind: Net margin contraction below 9% or unemployment reversing back below 3.9% (removing the defensive bid) would eliminate the rationale.
